text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In an interview with al-Hayat, President Hosni Mubarak said the economic conference would take place on time in Cairo and that he preferred not to postpone it so that no one could exploit that, but he called on the United States and Israel to do their utmost and make a positive move to change the current atmosphere and provide the confidence now lost because of the hardline statements coming out of Israel.
- Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Netanyahu's "nose" remark was unfortunate and said he would do better to keep off Egypt's nose so that Egypt keeps off his.

- Mubarak received an oral message from the Emir of Kuwait, conveyed by the Kuwaiti information minister, who said he briefed Mubarak on developments in Kuwait after the escalation of tension over Iraq.

- The cabinet will today discuss several reports which aim to encourage investment in Egypt. Cabinet Affairs Minister Talaat Hammad said the meeting would concentrate on abolishing some restrictions and some fees imposed on investment.

- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi said the security apparatus had identified the channels of finance for criminal groups inside Egypt and had obtained the "organisational map" of terror groups. He said the foreign media were trying to damage Egypt's reputation to divert tourism to other countries.

- Mubarak in interview with al-Hayat: For Arab states to cooperate with Israel economically, the atmosphere must be right. Egyptian public opinion is not in favour of normalisation but it is for a just peace. We oppose the partition of Iraq: America, Iran and Turkey also insist on the unity of Iraqi territory. The "Lebanon First" proposal will lead to limitless problems and put Lebanon in a difficult situation.

- Defence Minister Mohamed Hussein Tantawi watched the main stage of the strategic manoeuvres Badr 96, in which units from the second and third army corps took part. The main phase, which lasted more than four hours, included a tank battle.

- President Mubarak has made Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri the chairman of the Supreme Council for Youth and Sports. The old chairman, Abdel Moneim Emara, is now head of the council executive. The new council contains more than 10 ministers.

- Mubarak in interview with al-Hayat: Hardline statements from Israel undermine the success of the economic summit. America understands our position and we are not under pressure. Netanyahu wants to reconsider the agreements already signed and this is unacceptable.
- Communications Minister Soleiman Metwalli said 30,000 people have so far applied for mobile phones and that new applications can still be made. Tests on the mobile phone system have succeeded.
- The water level in Lake Nasser has fallen a centimetre at the High Dam, the first fall since this year's flood started.
